item.title: Door was locked at Pakistan hospital where fire killed 14 babies, witnesses say
item.description:
At least 14 babies at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences died in a nursery fire Wednesday, while one infant was rescued, according to hospital officials. The blaze at the major government hospital in the capital Islamabad broke out at about 6:45 a.m. after an air conditioning unit compressor exploded, hospital and rescue officials said. The fire was contained to the nursery in the hospital's gynecology ward and did not affect any other hospital wards. "One baby was rescued by a doctor," hospital spokesperson Dr. Aneeza Jalil said, adding that six of the deceased infants' bodies had been given over to families, while the remaining bodies would be given over soon. item.title: Canada Is Spending Billions to Help Its Workers Survive Our Tariffs
item.description:
On Tuesday, Canadian officials announced funding to back businesses, workers, and industries, as they implement dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs on the US in response to the Trump administration’s newly imposed 50 percent tariffs on roughly $20 billion worth of Canadian imports. Senior members of Canada’s government announced a support package worth $7.5 billion Canadian dollars, or about $5.4 billion US, including $3 million in non-repayable loans for every small business and a further $2 million in interest-free loans—even for businesses only indirectly affected by tariffs. Small and medium-sized businesses directly affected will be able to apply for a further $5 million through Canada’s business development bank, and the Canadian government has set aside $2 billion for medium-sized and large firms, more than half a billion dollars for retraining workers whose industries are affected…

item.title: Why Trump’s plan to rescind the Roadless Rule protecting national forests will struggle in court
item.description:
Roadless areas in Alaska contain important old-growth forests. Mike Reid Photography/Moment via Getty Images Over 368,000 miles of roads wind through U.S. national forests, eight times more than the entire interstate highway system . Many are heavily eroded and prone to landslides, and driving vehicles on them can spread invasive species. They need billions of dollars in repairs. Yet the Trump administration wants to build more roads in America’s national forests to expand timber production, specifically in untouched areas currently protected by the 2001 federal Roadless Rule . In announcing the administration’s formal proposal to rescind the Roadless Area Conservation Rule on Aug. 18, 2026, Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins argued that building roads in these areas is important for fighting wildfires. However, data show that roads actually tend to increase the risk of fires…

item.title: China denounces US threat of sanctions over trade with Iran
item.description:
Nearly six months into the U.S. war against Iran, one can’t help but come to the conclusion that President Donald Trump doesn’t know what he’s doing, is completely out of his depth, or is basing his policy on incredibly flawed assumptions. It brings to mind one of George Costanza’s famous quotes in ‘ Seinfeld ’: “Every decision I’ve ever made in my entire life has been wrong. My life is the complete opposite of everything I want it to be. Every instinct I have in every aspect of life, be it something to wear, something to eat, it’s all been wrong.” Subscribe now While this might seem overly hyperbolic, it doesn’t take a genius to recognize that every decision Trump makes with respect to Iran has led to results he didn’t expect. item.title: Dolly Parton never called herself a feminist. Her life made the case anyway.
item.description:
Dolly Parton, who used her stardom to not only embrace all listeners but also nurture marginalized communities through literacy and financial development, died peacefully in Nashville, Tennessee, on Tuesday, according to her family. She was 80. One of the best-selling musical artists of all time, Parton had 25 singles top the Billboard country music charts. She starred in blockbuster movies and beloved Christmas specials. Her theme park, Dollywood, is one of the most popular in the United States. Parton has been seen by many as a feminist icon, though she historically declined to use the word to describe herself. When podcaster Jad Abumrad asked the songwriter in 2019 if she thinks of herself as a feminist, she responded, “No, I do not. I think of myself as a woman in business.” Parton presented herself as a woman from a humble Appalachian beginning who pulled herself out of poverty…
